description: Implement pearl-precision crate: the Precision Decision Engine that classifies tasks as P0/P1/P2/P3 before execution based on their capability manifest declarations and quality spec. This is the step-level classification that determines which runtime adapter to route to (Article 1 enforcement). pearl-core already defines PrecisionClass and QualitySpec; this crate adds the decision logic that inspects a task's requirements and emits the classification.
steps: Create crates/pearl-precision/Cargo.toml with dependencies on pearl-core and pearl-governance (for CapabilityManifest). Use workspace.dependencies pattern.
Add pearl-precision to workspace members in /projects/sandbox/pearl/Cargo.toml and add pearl-precision = { path = 'crates/pearl-precision' } to [workspace.dependencies].
Create crates/pearl-precision/src/lib.rs with module doc explaining this enforces Article 1 (determinism first) and Article 11 (autonomy from verifiability) by classifying work before routing.
Implement a ClassificationInput struct that captures: capability_type, execution_kind, runtime, quality.deterministic, quality_spec (QualitySpec from pearl-core), and optional override.

Implement PrecisionDecisionEngine with a classify() method that applies the decision rules: (1) If quality.deterministic==true AND execution.kind==script AND runtime.is_mechanical() => P0. (2) If deterministic==false AND deterministic_verification==true => P1 (generative but verifiable). (3) If deterministic==false AND deterministic_verification==false AND exactness_required==true => P2 (partially verifiable). (4) Otherwise => P3 (subjective). Allow a manual override with audit trail.
Implement from_manifest(CapabilityManifest) -> ClassificationInput convenience method that extracts fields from a governance manifest.
Implement ClassificationResult with the class, reasoning (Vec<String> explaining which rules fired), and whether it was overridden.

Write comprehensive tests: P0 for deterministic scripts, P1 for LLM-generated-but-verifiable, P2 for exact-but-unverifiable, P3 for best-effort. Test override. Test that the classification aligns with Article 1 (P0 forbids LLM, checked via permits_llm_generation()).
Ensure cargo test --workspace passes, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.
acceptance_criteria: Classification of a deterministic script manifest yields P0
Classification of a non-deterministic manifest with deterministic verification yields P1
findings: All 252 workspace tests pass (20 new in pearl-precision). Clippy clean, fmt clean. The crate depends on pearl-core (PrecisionClass, QualitySpec) and pearl-governance (CapabilityManifest, ExecutionKind, Runtime, etc.). ClassificationInput::from_manifest and from_manifest_inferred provide two ways to construct input from governance manifests.
